note: Principle IV: >=80% line coverage across a feature's code, 100% for security-critical algorithmic code. `default` applies to every module in settings.gradle.kts. `overrides` sets one module's floor to something other than the default -- ABOVE it for code that must be held harder, or BELOW it as a starting floor you have already met and intend to raise. What is refused is going BACKWARDS: the push guard denies lowering `default`, lowering an existing override, and removing one, so a floor can only ever ratchet up. Set a starting floor to a number you have already measured, never to one you hope to reach -- an unmet floor denies every push. Coverage is measured with android-jvm-test-coverage for `jvm` modules and android-combined-test-coverage for `combined` and `instrumentation` ones, with connectedDebugAndroidTest executed on a device first, and compared against the exact value rather than the value rounded for display. Read by lib/coverage.py, which push-verify.sh gate 3 uses to deny a push and status.sh uses to report -- so an override naming a module you do not have is a dead key nothing reads. tools/prism-inventory.sh reports dead keys; prism-doctor does not look at this file at all. Write a floor as a whole number, or at most one decimal: a raw measurement pasted in here -- 98.30508474576271 -- claims a decision made to a ten-billionth of a percent about a number that moves with the next commit, and it breaks the eight-character required column in every report that prints it. lib/coverage.py floors anything longer to one decimal place, DOWNWARD, because rounding a floor up would deny the very push that measured it.
$example: The override below is an EXAMPLE, kept because a shape is easier to copy than to invent: it is what a security-critical module looks like. Replace ':core:crypto' with your own -- crypto, auth, payments, anything whose algorithm being wrong is worse than its being slow -- or delete the overrides object entirely. Deleting it is a supported answer and breaks no test.
